# October 2026 SLO reporting pack — Reliability Office, Brightwater Payments

Prepared 2026-11-02 by the Reliability Office for the monthly attainment report. Everything in this folder is a
copy; the live records are in the systems listed in the Reliability Office handbook.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `panel-catalogue-2026-10.json` | Widget definitions of the eight service boards (two per domain), exported by `boardctl` on 1 November. |
| `export_<board>_2026-10.csv` | One file per board: the daily value of each exported panel for 1–31 October 2026 (UTC days). Column names are widget ids from the catalogue. |
| `service-catalogue.csv` | The engineering service catalogue (owner, criticality, runtime, rotation). |
| `slo-definitions.yaml` | The SLI rule of every registered SLO (what makes a minute bad). |
| `reliability-office-handbook.md` | How the office works, where records live, the monthly cycle. |
| `monthly-reporting-runbook-v4.docx` | The step list analysts follow for the monthly report. |
| `error-budget-policy.docx` | What happens when an error budget runs low or out. |
| `reliability-review-minutes-2026-10-07.docx` | Minutes of the October reliability review. |
| `slo-report-2026-09.md` | The September report as published. |

## How the exports are produced

The nightly export job (`boardctl export`, run log beside this file) opens each service board and writes the daily
value of every exported panel exactly as the board shows it. Nothing is recomputed on export; values are in the unit
the widget declares in the catalogue. Days are UTC calendar days.

# Reliability Office handbook (rev. 7, 2026-09-29)

Owner: Ines Calloway, Head of Reliability Office. Analysts: Tobias Renwick, Noor Haddad.

## 1. What the office does
1.1 Publishes the monthly SLO attainment report for every SLO in the SLO register.
1.2 Raises one follow-up per missed objective in the owning team's Linear team.
1.3 Keeps the SLO register current (tiers, owners, nominated panels) between reviews.
1.4 Does not operate services, does not run incidents and does not speak to customers.

## 2. Where things live (systems of record)
| Record | System | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reliability standard RS-2 (targets, measurement, labels) | Confluence, space RELY | The only governing text for attainment. Amended by the reliability review; the wiki page is the edition in force. |
| SLO register | Airtable base "Reliability Office", table "SLO register" | Source of record for tier, owning team and nominated panel. Maintained live by the office. |
| Service boards, monitors | Datadog | Owned by the service teams and the observability platform. The office reads them and never edits them. |
| Maintenance declarations and incidents | PagerDuty | Declared windows are raised there by the owning team. |
| Change records | ServiceNow | Change approval. Owned by the change advisory board. |
| Planned maintenance calendar | Google Calendar (shared) | Planning only. |
| Cell topology, board conventions | Confluence, space PLAT | Owned by the platform team. |
| Follow-ups | Linear, one team per domain | Ledger Platform, Acquiring, Payouts, Risk Engineering. The office's own team (Reliability Office) is for office work, not follow-ups. |
| Monthly report | Confluence, space RELY | One page per month. |
| Customer status page | WordPress (status.brightwater-payments.example) | Owned by Customer Communications. Never written by the office. |

## 3. Monthly cycle
- Day 1–2: the export job runs; analysts check the pack.
- Day 2–4: compute attainment per RS-2, write the register's month fields, raise follow-ups.
- Day 5: publish the report page; the head of office replies to the VP Engineering.

## 4. Conventions
4.1 The register's month fields are numbers (attainment as a percentage, budget remaining in minutes) and a status
label copied from RS-2.
4.2 A nominated panel is the panel an owning team chose to display its SLO on its board. Teams change their boards
without telling us; the register lags.
4.3 Since the September rebuild (board-rebuild-notes-2026-09.md) every service board is templated; see the platform
team's conventions page.
4.4 Analysts work from the exports in the pack; the monitoring server is there to answer questions about them.

## 5. History that explains a convention
- Until June 2026 attainment was request-based; RS-2 moved to bad minutes in July 2026 so that low-traffic services
  are not flattered by quiet nights.
- Tier 3 was introduced in August 2026 for back-office services.
- In September 2026 statement-render moved from Tier 3 to Tier 2 (customer statements are now on the merchant
  dashboard); the register carries the change from 1 October.

# October draft — working notes (Tobias Renwick, 2026-11-02)

Ines — I got most of October done before my leave; picking up is yours. Draft numbers in
october-attainment-draft-trenwick.csv. Nothing written to the register or Linear yet.

## Method (same as September)
- Each SLO from its nominated panel (register), summed from the board exports.
- fx-rates-feed, 3ds-challenge and chargeback-intake panels are in seconds: divided by 60 (lesson from July).
- ledger-posting 14 Oct and fraud-score 6 Oct: declared in PagerDuty days ahead -> excluded from eligible and bad.
- card-auth-gateway 21 Oct: Felix raised the PagerDuty record at 10:40, after the work. Left in, per the August reversal.
- tokenisation-vault 27 Oct key rotation: only on the shared calendar and in chat, never raised in PagerDuty. Left in.
- sanctions-screen 18 Oct window was cancelled the day before; nothing to exclude.

## Result
5 of 20 objectives missed by my count. Gideon has seen the headline and is happy it is in line with September.

## Open
- Linear follow-ups and the report page are not started.
- sweep-reconciler is Tier 3, so its budget is large; no need to chase it.

# Service boards v3 rebuild — notes (Soren Blackwood, Observability Platform, 2026-09-18)

## Why
Per-cell copies of every board (one per production cell plus the canary) had drifted. v3 keeps one board per
audience and adds template variables instead.

## What changed
1. Every service board has two template variables: `$cell` (values: kestrel-1, kestrel-2, kestrel-3, kestrel-*, wren-0)
   and `$region` (eu-west-1 only for now).
2. Every SLO widget's query carries `$cell` and `$region`; no widget pins a cell except the explicit canary widgets on
   the Acquiring board.
3. Board owners choose and save their boards' views; observability does not reset them.
4. The nightly export job exports SLO widgets from every service board.
5. Board ids stay the same as v2 so the SLO register's nominated panels did not need re-pointing.

## Known gaps
- Two boards per domain: the domain's service board and its on-call board. Titles are close; ids differ.

RS-2 Service level objectives — reliability standard
Edition 6, in force from 2026-08-01. Owner: Reliability Office. Approved by the reliability review.

1. Scope
1.1 This standard governs the monthly attainment of every SLO listed in the SLO register.
1.2 Where any runbook, board, draft or earlier report differs from this standard, this standard governs.

2. Measurement period and eligible minutes
2.1 The measurement period is the calendar month in UTC.
2.2 Eligible minutes are the minutes of the period less the minutes of declared maintenance windows (section 5).

3. The SLI of record
3.1 Each SLO counts bad minutes by the rule in its SLI definition.
3.2 Bad minutes are counted on the production serving path: the customer traffic served by the production cells
taken together. The SLI of record is the service as customers reach it across the whole production fleet.
3.3 Traffic served by the canary cell during a release soak is pre-release exposure. It is not part of the SLI of
record. Neither is any single production cell taken on its own.

4. Targets
4.1 The target of an SLO is set by its tier: Tier 1 99.95 %, Tier 2 99.90 %, Tier 3 99.50 %.
4.2 The tier of record is the tier on the SLO's register entry. Catalogue criticality is a paging attribute and does
not set targets.

5. Maintenance windows
5.1 A maintenance window is declared when the owning team raises it in PagerDuty (the incident tool) against the
service, stating the window, before the window opens. An approved change record is an approval, not a declaration.
5.2 The minutes of a declared window leave the measurement: they are removed from the eligible minutes and from the
bad minutes. (A service is drained for a declared window, so its SLI records every minute of the window as bad.)
5.3 Planned work that was not declared before it began is ordinary downtime and stays in both counts, whatever a
calendar, a chat message or a later record says. A declared window that was cancelled removes nothing.

6. Error budget
6.1 Allowed bad minutes = (1 - target) x eligible minutes.
6.2 Budget remaining = allowed bad minutes - bad minutes. It is negative when the objective is missed.
6.3 All figures are in minutes. Bad time reported in another unit is converted to minutes first.

7. Status labels (use exactly)
7.1 "Objective met" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining at least 25 % of allowed bad minutes.
7.2 "Objective met — budget at risk" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining below 25 % of allowed.
7.3 "Objective missed" - attainment below target.

8. Figures and rounding
8.1 Attainment % = (eligible minutes - bad minutes) / eligible minutes x 100.
8.2 Attainment is recorded to three decimal places and budget remaining to one decimal place, rounded half away from
zero. Status is decided on the unrounded figures.

9. Follow-ups
9.1 Each missed objective gets exactly one follow-up issue in the owning team's tracker for the month.

10. Records
10.1 The SLO register is the source of record for tier and owning team and is maintained live by the Reliability
Office. Its nominated panel is the owning team's display choice.
10.2 The monthly report page is published in the RELY space once the register's month fields are complete.

Serving cells and release rings (Platform Engineering, rev. 2026-09-15)

Production cells
- kestrel-1, kestrel-2, kestrel-3: the production serving fleet in eu-west-1. Every customer request is load-balanced
  across the three. In Datadog tags they are cell:kestrel-1, cell:kestrel-2, cell:kestrel-3; cell:kestrel-* matches all
  three together.

Canary cell
- wren-0: ring 0 of the release train. Every release soaks on wren-0 for 24 hours on opt-in canary merchants before it
  is promoted to the kestrel cells (release soak procedure). wren-0 serves roughly 1.5-2.5 % of requests during a soak
  and none when it is drained. Tag: cell:wren-0, ring:canary.

Rings
- ring 0 (canary): wren-0
- ring 1 (production): kestrel-1, kestrel-2, kestrel-3

Notes
- wren-0 reads from staging copies of some stores (document bucket, rules cache), so its failures and the production
  cells' failures are not the same events.
- Region template variable: eu-west-1 is the only region in service in 2026.

Service boards — templating conventions (v3, Observability Platform, 2026-09-18)

1. Every service board carries two template variables, $cell and $region. Allowed $cell values: kestrel-1, kestrel-2,
   kestrel-3, kestrel-* and wren-0.
2. Widget queries use the variables; a widget shows whatever the variables are set to.
3. A board opens, and is exported, with its saved view: the variable values its owners last saved.
4. Owners choose their saved views. Observability does not reset them.
5. The only widgets that pin a cell are the canary widgets on the Acquiring service board (cell:wren-0).
6. Board ids are stable; titles are owner-chosen free text.

output.title: RS-2 Service level objectives — reliability standard

storage.value:
RS-2 Service level objectives — reliability standard
Edition 6, in force from 2026-08-01. Owner: Reliability Office. Approved by the reliability review.

1. Scope
1.1 This standard governs the monthly attainment of every SLO listed in the SLO register.
1.2 Where any runbook, board, draft or earlier report differs from this standard, this standard governs.

2. Measurement period and eligible minutes
2.1 The measurement period is the calendar month in UTC.
2.2 Eligible minutes are the minutes of the period less the minutes of declared maintenance windows (section 5).

3. The SLI of record
3.1 Each SLO counts bad minutes by the rule in its SLI definition.
3.2 Bad minutes are counted on the production serving path: the customer traffic served by the production cells
taken together. The SLI of record is the service as customers reach it across the whole production fleet.
3.3 Traffic served by the canary cell during a release soak is pre-release exposure. It is not part of the SLI of
record. Neither is any single production cell taken on its own.

4. Targets
4.1 The target of an SLO is set by its tier: Tier 1 99.95 %, Tier 2 99.90 %, Tier 3 99.60 %.
    (For August and September 2026 the Tier 3 target was 99.50 %.)
4.2 The tier of record is the tier on the SLO's register entry. Catalogue criticality is a paging attribute and does
not set targets.

5. Maintenance windows
5.1 A maintenance window is declared when the owning team raises it in PagerDuty (the incident tool) against the
service, stating the window, before the window opens. An approved change record is an approval, not a declaration.
5.2 The minutes of a declared window leave the measurement: they are removed from the eligible minutes and from the
bad minutes. (A service is drained for a declared window, so its SLI records every minute of the window as bad.)
5.3 Planned work that was not declared before it began is ordinary downtime and stays in both counts, whatever a
calendar, a chat message or a later record says. A declared window that was cancelled removes nothing.

6. Error budget
6.1 Allowed bad minutes = (1 - target) x eligible minutes.
6.2 Budget remaining = allowed bad minutes - bad minutes. It is negative when the objective is missed.
6.3 All figures are in minutes. Bad time reported in another unit is converted to minutes first.

7. Status labels (use exactly)
7.1 "Objective met" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining at least 25 % of allowed bad minutes.
7.2 "Objective met — budget at risk" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining below 25 % of allowed.
7.3 "Objective missed" - attainment below target.

8. Figures and rounding
8.1 Attainment % = (eligible minutes - bad minutes) / eligible minutes x 100.
8.2 Attainment is recorded to three decimal places and budget remaining to one decimal place, rounded half away from
zero. Status is decided on the unrounded figures.

9. Follow-ups
9.1 Each missed objective gets exactly one follow-up issue in the owning team's tracker for the month.

10. Records
10.1 The SLO register is the source of record for tier and owning team and is maintained live by the Reliability
Office. Its nominated panel is the owning team's display choice.
10.2 The monthly report page is published in the RELY space once the register's month fields are complete.

Corrigenda
C1 (2026-11-03, reliability review). Section 4.1 corrected. Edition 6 was approved with a Tier 3 target of
99.50 % for its first two months (August and September 2026) and 99.60 % from 1 October 2026. The page was not
updated on 1 October and still showed 99.50 %. The corrected target applies to every month from October 2026.
Entered by Noor Haddad for the review; checked against the edition 6 approval record by Anouk Verhaegen.
Q: does a PagerDuty incident raised by a monitor during planned work count as a declaration? A (Ines): no, section 5.1 needs the team to raise the window before it opens.
Checked C1 against the edition 6 approval record from the review: Tier 3 steps from 99.50 % to 99.60 % on 1 October 2026. October is the first month on 99.60 %.

Which panels I used and which I set aside
- RS-2 section 3 counts bad minutes on the production serving path: the production cells kestrel-1, kestrel-2 and kestrel-3 taken together (cell:kestrel-*). wren-0 is the canary cell (ring 0 of the release train); its soak traffic is pre-release exposure and does not count, and neither does a single production cell on its own.
- Every board is templated on $cell, and the export job pulls each board with its saved view, so a panel shows whatever cell its board is saved on, whatever the board's title or the register's nomination says. The board records on the monitoring server show the saved views.
- The Payouts service board ("Payouts · Service SLOs", bwp-pay-svc), which the register nominates for all five Payouts SLOs (payout-scheduler, bank-file-dispatch, payee-verification, payout-status-api, sweep-reconciler), is saved on the canary cell wren-0, so I set its panels aside and took the Payouts figures from the Payouts on-call board (bwp-pay-oncall), which is saved on all production cells (kestrel-*). payee-verification's nominated panel was set aside too, although its figures come out the same on both boards.
- The Risk on-call board (bwp-rsk-oncall), which the register nominates for dispute-evidence and kyc-document-check, is also saved on wren-0, so those two SLOs come from the Risk service board (bwp-rsk-svc), saved on kestrel-*.
- The Ledger on-call board (bwp-led-oncall, kestrel-1) and the Acquiring on-call board (bwp-acq-oncall, kestrel-2) each show a single production cell, so I did not use them. The Acquiring board titled "Canary & SLO watch" (bwp-acq-svc) is in fact saved on all production cells; its SLO panels were used despite the title (only its separate fixed canary widgets pin wren-0).
- Why the canary panels mislead: the 19 October payouts outage hit the production cells while the canary cell was drained (17-20 October after the 4.19.2 rollback), so the canary-scoped Payouts panels understate payout-scheduler's and sweep-reconciler's bad minutes; the 8 October document-bucket outage hit the production cells but not the canary cell, so the canary-scoped Risk on-call panels understate kyc-document-check's (and dispute-evidence's) bad minutes. The other way round, bank-file-dispatch and payout-status-api show more bad minutes on the canary-scoped panels (soak failures on wren-0) than on production, which would have shown a breach that does not exist on the production serving path.
